reply:
Here is the same information again, in plain words, using the terms from `GLOSSARY.md`.

## The context

Your task runs as a **Graph**. A Graph is a set of **Nodes**, and a Node is one step in the Graph. The Graph moves from one Node to the next Node.

Right now the Graph stops at one Node. This Node asks for your approval before it does the rest of the work.

## What happens after you approve

1. The system saves a **Checkpoint**. A Checkpoint is a saved record of the Graph state. It says which Node must run next.
2. The system reads this Checkpoint. It uses it to link your approval to the Node that waited for your approval.
3. The Graph starts again at this Node. It then runs the next Node.
4. The last Node writes the report. You then get the report.

So the Checkpoint is what makes the Graph continue. The Graph does not start again at the first Node. It starts again at the Node where it stopped.

## One warning

A Checkpoint does not guarantee that an external action happens only once.

If the system stops after it saves the Checkpoint but before it writes the report, the system writes the report two times when it starts again. This can happen because the report is a file outside the Graph.

Therefore, after the task ends, check the report file. If the file contains the report two times, remove the copy that is not correct.
